Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberFortress Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing up questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberFortress Inc.'s results for the second quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Alex Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Mark Harlan, Chief Security Officer; Lisa Chen, VP of Sales; David Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and Rachel Kim, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Reyes.

Johnathan Reyes: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. CyberFortress delivered exceptional results in the second quarter, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. Our performance reflects the strength of our product portfolio, our expanding customer base, and our commitment to innovation. The adoption rate of Sentinel AI is accelerating, demonstrating its transformative impact in delivering sub-30-second mean time to respond and the unmatched value we bring to our customers.

Progress on our key strategic initiatives has been the cornerstone of this outperformance. We're not just keeping pace with the cybersecurity arms race—we're pulling ahead, fueled by surging demand for AI-native defenses against a 42% year-over-year rise in global ransomware incidents, as noted by Chainalysis, and the ongoing ripples from supply chain breaches reminiscent of SolarWinds and Log4j.

Let me outline our four core pillars and the quantifiable advancements we've made. First, our AI/ML-powered autonomous threat response. Sentinel AI, now in its third generation, harnesses generative AI and federated learning to slash MTTR by 65% year-over-year. Q2 ARR from Sentinel AI surged 78% to $142 million, making up 28% of total recurring revenue. The proprietary Swarm Intelligence engine correlates behavioral analytics across endpoints, networks, and cloud workloads, cutting false positives by 82% versus traditional SIEM solutions. We've secured 14 deals exceeding $5 million ACV, including a critical deployment for a Fortune 10 financial firm that stopped a nation-state phishing operation in real time, averting $200 million in potential wire fraud. R&D spend is at 18% of revenue, enabling MITRE ATT&CK integrations and the Predictive Hunt module, which anticipates zero-day exploits at 91% accuracy using dark web signals.

Second, expansion of our cloud-native Zero Trust platform. As enterprises rush to SASE—projected by Gartner to reach $27 billion by 2027—Fortress Zero embeds micro-segmentation and adaptive trust into AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. Cloud security bookings grew 112% YoY, lifting cloud ARR to $210 million or 42% of total. Net revenue retention here is 128%, with customers consolidating vendors. A standout was our $48 million multi-year SASE contract with a top-5 U.S. healthcare provider amid HIPAA demands. Our identity fabric cuts lateral movement risks by 95%, integrating seamlessly with Okta and Ping for passwordless access, keeping churn below 2%.

Third, OT/ICS security for critical infrastructure, our fastest-growing area, riding CISA mandates after Colonial Pipeline and a 300% jump in ICS exploits per Dragos. The ICS Sentinel suite, tailored for Purdue Model Levels 0-3, generated $89 million in Q2 ARR, up 145% YoY, with physics-aware ML spotting anomalies in Modbus and DNP3 protocols. North America led with 62% of wins, including major energy players, while EMEA doubled on NIS2 tailwinds in German manufacturing. We've neutralized over 1,200 OT threats year-to-date, trimming recovery times dramatically, with 92% gross margins thanks to high entry barriers.

Finally, global market penetration via strategic partnerships. APAC exploded 167% YoY to $67 million, boosted by digital banking in Southeast Asia and China's CSRC rules akin to Singapore's PDPA. Deals with NTT in Japan and Tencent Cloud yielded 25 joint proofs-of-concept converting at 72%. EMEA unlocked 34 deals under GDPR and DORA, and LATAM pilots with major banks point to 50% H2 upside. Our $120 million acquisition of a Tel Aviv behavioral biometrics firm strengthens UEBA to rival CrowdStrike Falcon and Microsoft Defender.

These efforts set us up for 35-40% organic growth in 2024, beating Gartner's 14.5% cybersecurity CAGR. We're grabbing share in the $50 billion EDR/NGAV space with 2.3x better efficacy per AV-TEST. We manage AI ethics risks through audit logs and counter macro pressures with 85% recurring revenue and $450 million in cash for M&A.

Our strategic priorities also encompass robust new customer acquisition, accelerating ARR growth both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year, recent product and feature launches, a highly effective go-to-market strategy, glowing customer feedback on innovations, optimized marketing spend efficiency, and stellar channel partner performance contributing significantly to revenue. Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. We achieved record revenue of $650 million in the second quarter, representing a 55% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained strong at 82%, and we continued to invest aggressively in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $420 million. Net income was $120 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.85. We are increasing our full-year revenue guidance to $2.6 billion to $2.7 billion and earnings guidance accordingly, based on our strong performance to date.

Customer acquisition momentum further highlights our platform's strength in this competitive arena. In Q2, we added 478 net new customers, up 32% year-over-year and 12% sequentially from Q1's 427, bringing our total base to over 8,200. Fortune 1000 customers grew 28% YoY to 42% of logos. Enterprise wins (ACV over $100K) hit 132, up 45%, including a top-5 global bank integrating our AI-native EDR with Okta and AWS. Mid-market and SMB added 256, up 25%, via MSSP channels like Optiv and TD SYNNEX, with our unified XDR enabling SOC-as-a-Service. Government added 90, including U.S. federal CMMC deals.

Regionally, U.S./Canada took 62%, EMEA 22% on GDPR/NIS2, APAC 38% YoY on sovereign clouds, LATAM 9% via resellers. Aegis Shield AI drove 40% of wins, cutting MTTD 65%; OT/IoT expansions closed 15 industrial deals. New ACV rose 18% to $78K, NRR 118%, win rates 62%. We guide 500-550 new customers in Q3.

Turning to ARR, total ARR ended Q2 at $1.28 billion, up 18% QoQ from $1.085 billion and 52% YoY from $842 million—our 11th straight QoQ acceleration, topping peer averages. DBNER held at 128%. QoQ came from eight $10M+ deals, like a $45 million CyberMesh SASE pact with a Fortune 10 firm, plus $120 million expansions into GenAI modules amid 300% AI threat growth. Sales cycles shortened to 45 days via hyperscaler channels at 35% of bookings. YoY reflected ransomware and regs like NIS2/SEC rules, with 65% win rates vs. Prisma/SentinelOne. Public sector ARR up 78% to $185 million on FedRAMP. North America 62% of ARR at 55% YoY, EMEA 68% to $320 million, APAC 85% to $210 million, LATAM 22%. AutoRemediate blocks 98% zero-days in seconds per MITRE. Guide Q3 16-19% QoQ, FY 48-50% YoY.

Channel partners were pivotal, contributing 72% of Q2 revenue or $205 million at $285 million total implied recurring—up 28% YoY, 12% QoQ, outpacing direct 18% YoY. Over 4,200 deal registrations converted 62%, average ACV $1.2 million. Top 20 partners like CDW/Insight did 45%, NRR over 125%. Partner Accelerator cut ramp 40%; GenAI certifications boosted MSP wins 15% vs. Cortex. Hyperscalers: AWS 22% channel ARR, Azure +40%. Americas 55% channel at 32% YoY, EMEA 28% at 25%, APAC 17% at 42%. Guide $850-900 million FY channel, targeting 75% mix.

Now, over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Alex. Our technology team is focused on developing cutting-edge security solutions that leverage the latest advancements in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas include our recent product and feature launches amid a 28% YoY ransomware rise per Verizon DBIR and nation-state threats like Change Healthcare. In Q2, we rolled out three major updates driving 42% QoQ new product bookings to $187 million or 35% ARR.

NexusXDR 4.0 integrates generative AI on 15 petabytes of telemetry for predictive drift detection (94% true positives, 18% edge over Falcon per MITRE), SOAR playbooks slashing MTTR 68%, with 1,200 subscriptions at $92 million ARR, 145% NRR—68% NA, EMEA +55% via Deutsche Telekom.

ZeroTrust Edge 2.5 adds NIST Kyber quantum-resistant crypto, adaptive identity fabric (89% access reduction), SSE inspection at <10ms on 150 PoPs, AWS Bedrock integrations—$68 million bookings, APAC +112%.

OTShield Industrial maps Purdue Levels 0-2, converges IT/OT XDR—450 customers, $27 million ARR, 82% NA.

Features: NexusAI Copilot accelerates triage 55%, SupplyChain Sentinel scans SBOMs for 1,200 CVEs. R&D at 22% revenue positions our 1:3 expansion ratio ahead.

Thank you. Over to Mark Harlan.

Mark Harlan: Security remains our top priority. We are continuously monitoring the threat landscape and adapting our security posture to protect our customers and our own infrastructure, with transparent audit logs and proactive measures against AI ethics and regulatory risks.

Lisa Chen: We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is focused on building strong relationships with our customers and partners and expanding our market share through precision targeting and land-and-expand motions.

David Patel: Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. We are using a variety of channels to reach our target audience, including digital marketing, public relations, and events. We are also investing in thought leadership initiatives to establish CyberFortress as a trusted advisor in the cybersecurity industry. On spend efficiency, we hit 6.2x ROI in Q2 on $48.7 million or 18.2% revenue—up from 4.8x QoQ, down 220bps YoY. CAC fell 28% QoQ to $11,400, LTV/CAC 4.1x. Digital shift to 62% budget drove 47% MQLs, 32% SQL conversion via "Zero-Trust Horizon." AI lead scoring cut MQL-to-won 35%; ABM for top 500 at 48% wins. NA ROI 7.1x, EMEA 5.4x, APAC 6.8x. Threat-led campaigns like "Shieldwall" generated $22 million pipeline; partners 45% influenced. Guide Q4 6.5x+ ROI.

Rachel Kim: Thank you. Our product strategy focuses on delivering innovative and integrated security solutions that address the evolving needs of our customers. We are constantly gathering feedback from our customers and partners to ensure that our products meet their needs and exceed their expectations. Feedback on NexusXDR 2.0 and EdgeSecure Pro has been outstanding: 94% CSAT, NPS 68, beating Gartner 82%. 62% upsell in 90 days added $28 million ARR, churn <2%, NRR 98%. UEBA flagged 73% more insiders; SOC fatigue down 55%. 99.99% uptime, regional NPS high in APAC 72. Roadmap accelerates GenAI SOAR, integrations with Slack/ServiceNow at 91% satisfaction.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press star then one if you have a question. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Carter: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you expand on the ARR acceleration drivers, especially QoQ versus YoY components?

Johnathan Reyes: Thanks, Emily. As Alex detailed, the 18% QoQ blended large logos like the $45 million CyberMesh deal with expansions into GenAI amid exploding threats, shorter cycles via channels, and 128% NRR. YoY 52% rode regulatory tailwinds and platform wins, positioning us ahead in $150 billion TAM.

Operator: Next question from Mike Larson with Morgan Stanley.

Mike Larson: Great results. On new customers, how sustainable is the 32% YoY, and any vertical shifts?

Alex Rivera: Absolutely sustainable, Mike. Enterprise up 45% on regulated sectors, mid-market 25% channel-driven, government strong on CMMC. ACV expansion to $78K and 118% NRR support ongoing 30%+ growth, guiding 500+ in Q3.

Operator: Next from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: Impressive launches. How are NexusXDR and OTShield performing in early customer deployments?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Strong traction, Raj. NexusXDR at 145% NRR with MTTR cuts, OTShield securing energy/manufacturing with converged visibility. Beta metrics exceed MITRE benchmarks, fueling 35% ARR contribution.

Operator: Next from Laura Kim with Barclays.

Laura Kim: Thanks. Channels at 72%—any partner concentration risks or APAC upside details?

Mark Harlan: No major risks, Laura. Top partners stable at 45%, diversified regionally—APAC +42% via Datacom/Tech Data on SASE. Elite MSP program doubles partner growth, targeting 75% mix.

Johnathan Reyes: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create value for our shareholders. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
